meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of حلو ('sweet, lovely').

examples.trans: It has the loveliest view of the courtyard.
This is the nicest day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine form of أم ('mother'); إمي means 'my mother'.

examples.text: إمي بتعمل أطيب مربى مشمش بالصيف.
examples.trans: My mother makes the best apricot jam in summer.

examples.text: سلم على إمك لما ترجع عالبيت.
examples.trans: Say hello to your mother when you get home.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Saturday (يوم السبت or simply السبت), start of the Jordanian working/market weekend.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: As a noun after على (على بعد عشر أمتار 'at a distance of ten metres'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: The shop is five minutes away.
The stop is a hundred metres away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from جبل ('mountain'); عسل جبلي ('mountain honey') is dark, aromatic wildflower honey.

examples.text: العسل الجبلي لونه غامق وطعمه غني.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a dark colour and a rich taste.
The mountain air in Amman cools down at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Season name ('autumn'); بالخريف means 'in autumn'.

examples.text: ورق الشجر بالساحة بيصير أصفر بالخريف.
examples.trans: The tree leaves in the courtyard turn yellow in autumn.

examples.text: أول مطر بالخريف بيغسل حجر الياسمين.
examples.trans: The first rain in autumn washes the stone around the jasmine.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine hollow verb (from Classical ذاق, with ذ -> د); imperative دوق / دوقي ('taste!').

examples.text: دوقي هالمربى الحلو قبل ما نشتري المرطبان.
examples.trans: Taste this sweet jam before we buy the jar.
Ziad tasted the honey and smiled right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدفع, بيدفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
I paid for both valves in cash!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: روايح.

examples.trans: The aroma of coffee in the morning is wonderful!
The scent of cinnamon reaches the second floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زوايا.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'extra' (قطع زيادة extra pieces, الدرج الزيادة the extra stairs).

examples.trans: I brought two extra chairs for the courtyard.
I put a little extra mint in the tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سلال.

examples.trans: I put the yellow lemons in the basket.
He tossed the paper into the wastebasket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسواق.

examples.text: سوق وسط البلد مليان حركة الصبح.
examples.trans: The downtown market is bustling in the morning.
We bought fresh herbs from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشم, بيشم).

examples.trans: Smell that wonderful aroma in the kitchen!
We smelled the cinnamon from the stairs.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Used in the universal morning greeting صباح الخير ('good morning'), answered with صباح النور.

examples.trans: Good morning! How did you sleep today?
The weather is very pleasant this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامقة, plural: غامقين).

examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: Describes a wealthy person as well as rich flavours, colours, or musical tones (طعم غني 'rich taste').

examples.text: عسل الجبل طعمه غني ودافي مع الشاي.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a rich, warm taste with tea.

examples.text: خشب الجوز بيعطي البيانو صوت غني.
examples.trans: Walnut wood gives the piano a rich sound.

meanings.note: Handcrafted fired clay vessels and cups, a staple of Jordanian and Levantine street markets.

examples.text: اشترينا إبريق وفناجين من بسطة الفخار.
examples.trans: We bought a pitcher and cups from the pottery stall.

examples.text: المي ببريق الفخار بتضل باردة بالصيف.
examples.trans: Water in a clay pitcher stays cool in summer.

meanings.note: Covers both sweet fruit tarts (فطاير ليمون 'lemon tarts') and savoury baked pastries; Levantine plural فطاير.

examples.text: سلمى رح تخبز فطاير ليمون طازة ليوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Salma is going to bake fresh lemon tarts for Friday.

examples.text: ريحة الفطاير السخنة واصلة لباب النزل.
examples.trans: The aroma of hot pastries reaches the inn door.

meanings.note: Everyday market word for coins and small notes given back as change.

examples.text: معك فكة عشرة دنانير لو سمحت؟
examples.trans: Do you have change for ten dinars, please?

examples.text: ضل معنا فكة بكيس الكاش بعد السوق.
examples.trans: We still had coins to spare in the cash pouch after the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of زجاج ('glass').

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Singulative of collective قشر ('peel, bark, shell'); قشرة الليمونة means 'the skin/zest of the lemon'.

examples.text: قشرة الليمون الأصفر ريحتها قوية وحلوة.
examples.trans: Yellow lemon peel has a strong, sweet scent.

examples.text: بتحط سلمى برش قشرة ليمون بعجينة الكيك.
examples.trans: Salma puts grated lemon peel into the cake batter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I paid the bill in cash at the shop.
Do you prefer paying cash or card?

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Intransitive verb (past كبرت kbirt 'I grew up') from the root ك-ب-ر ('big, great').

examples.text: زياد ورامي كبروا قريب من سوق السبت.
examples.trans: Ziad and Rami grew up near the Saturday market.

examples.text: شجرة الياسمين كبرت ووصلت للطابق التاني.
examples.trans: The jasmine tree grew and reached the second floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: In questions كم + singular noun asks 'how many?'; in statements كم + singular noun means 'a few' (كم دقيقة 'a few minutes').

examples.trans: Give him a few minutes, Rami.

examples.text: كم لفة قرفة بيقدر فرنك يخبز؟
examples.trans: How many cinnamon rolls can your oven bake?

meanings.note: Stays invariable after numbers in everyday market speech: تلاتة كيلو ليمون ('three kilos of lemons').

examples.text: اعطيني اتنين كيلو تفاح أحمر لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Give me two kilos of red apples, please.

examples.text: تلاتة كيلو ليمون بيكفوا لكل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Three kilos of lemons are enough for the whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلاقي, بيلاقي).

examples.trans: Tell me how to find the hardware shop.

examples.text: لقيت هاد الصندوق الخشب ورا الحيط!
examples.trans: I found this wooden box behind the wall!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a glass jam, honey, or olive jar (dual مرطبانين, plural مرطبانات).

examples.trans: We lined the jars of jam and honey up on the shelf.
Open the new jar of honey for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمطار.

examples.trans: Please come inside out of the cold rain.
The trees are green and lovely after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: In spoken Jordanian, standard ملعقة shifts consonants to معلقة (ma'laqa), plural معالق (ma'aaliq).

examples.text: حطي معلقة صغيرة جنب كل فنجان.
examples.trans: Put a small spoon beside every cup.
The silver spoons are in the top drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: From ميزان ('scales, balance'); everyday word for a household or project budget.

examples.text: اشترينا كل الأغراض وضلينا ضمن الميزانية.
examples.trans: We bought all the supplies and stayed within budget.
Nour worked out the café budget in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمشي, بيمشي).

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.

examples.text: اسمع، المي عم بتمشي جوا الماسورة!
examples.trans: Listen, the water is flowing inside the pipe!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Tea with fresh mint warms the heart.
We planted mint in the courtyard beside the tree.

meanings.note: Imperative-only verb in everyday Arabic, inflected for gender and number: هات (to a man), هاتي (to a woman), هاتوا (plural).

examples.text: هات السلة التقيلة عنك يا أستاذ مازن.
examples.trans: Give me that heavy basket for you, Mr Mazen.

examples.text: هاتي القلم الرصاص من على المكتب يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me the pencil from the desk, Nour.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ورد.

examples.trans: We walked past the flower stall.
The scent of roses and jasmine filled the courtyard.

meanings.note: Form II verb from و-ف-ر; active participle موفر / موفرين ('saving, ahead on budget').

examples.text: خصم الدزينة وفر علينا مبلغ حلو.
examples.trans: The dozen discount saved us a nice amount.

examples.text: لما ندهن الشيش بإيدنا بنوفر بالميزانية.
examples.trans: When we paint the shutters ourselves, we save on the budget.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
